1.1: So in the very first year Cyrus was king over Persia, the Lord stirred somethin' in his spirit—just like Jeremiah said would happen. Cyrus made a big public announcement across the land and even wrote it down.
1.2: This what King Cyrus of Persia said: 'The Lord God of heaven done gave me all the kingdoms on earth, and He told me to build Him a house in Jerusalem, in Judah.'
1.3: 'So who among y'all belong to His people? If your God with you, go head and roll out to Jerusalem in Judah and rebuild the Lord's house—the God of Israel. That's the real God, and His house in Jerusalem.'
1.4: 'And if y'all ain't goin' but still live around here, help the ones who are. Give 'em silver, gold, goods, animals—whatever. And don't forget the freewill offerings for God's house in Jerusalem.'
1.5: Then the leaders of Judah and Benjamin, plus the priests and Levites—everybody who felt God moving in their heart—got up and said, 'Bet. We gon' go build the Lord's house in Jerusalem.'
1.6: The people around them didn't just stand by—they showed love. Gave 'em silver, gold, goods, livestock, and valuable gifts. And on top of that, some folks just gave because they wanted to.
1.7: King Cyrus even brought out all the stuff that used to be in God's house—the ones Nebuchadnezzar stole from Jerusalem and put up in his false god's temple.
1.8: Cyrus had his treasurer, Mithredath, hand over everything to a dude named Sheshbazzar, who was the prince of Judah.
1.9: Here's what they counted out: thirty gold plates, a thousand silver plates, twenty-nine knives,
1.10: thirty gold bowls, four hundred and ten silver bowls (all kinds), and a thousand other things.
1.11: Altogether, it was 5,400 gold and silver items. Sheshbazzar took all that with him when he and the exiles dipped outta Babylon and headed back to Jerusalem.

2.1: Now look—these the folks from the province who came back home after gettin' snatched up in captivity. Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, had deported 'em, but they made their way back to Jerusalem and Judah, each one to their own hometown.
2.2: They came up with Zerubbabel—Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispar, Bigvai, Rehum, and Baanah led the way. Now here go the roll call of the Israelites who returned:
2.6: From the fam of Pahath-Moab (descendants of Jeshua and Joab)—2,812.
2.16: From the fam of Ater, the ones linked to Hezekiah—98.
2.25: From Kirjath Arim, Chephirah, and Beeroth—743.
2.36: Here go the priests: sons of Jedaiah from the line of Jeshua—973.
2.40: Now the Levites: sons of Jeshua and Kadmiel, from Hodaviah's folks—74.
2.42: Gatekeepers: sons of Shallum, Ater, Talmon, Akkub, Hatita, and Shobai—139 in total.
2.43: The Temple workers (a.k.a. Nethinim): sons of Ziha, Hasupha, Tabbaoth,
2.55: Now the folks who served Solomon back in the day: sons of Sotai, Sophereth, Peruda,
2.57: Shephatiah, Hattil, Pochereth of Zebaim, and Ami.
2.58: Altogether, the Temple workers and Solomon's servants came out to 392.
2.59: Some folks pulled up from Tel Melah, Tel Harsha, Cherub, Addan, and Immer—but they ain't have no receipts. Couldn't prove who they people were or if they was really Israelites.
2.60: These included the sons of Delaiah, Tobiah, and Nekoda—652 total.
2.61: Even some priestly families had that problem: sons of Habaiah, sons of Koz, and the sons of Barzillai (who married into that Gileadite Barzillai fam and took the name).
2.62: They tried to find themselves in the records, but came up short—so they got cut off from priest duties 'cause they couldn't prove they was legit.
2.63: The governor told 'em they wasn't allowed to eat the sacred priest food until a priest could check in with God using the Urim and Thummim (holy tools for guidance).
2.64: All the people who came back added up to 42,360.
2.65: Not counting their crew—they had 7,337 male and female servants. Oh, and 200 singers—men and women.
2.66: They came through with 736 horses, 245 mules,
2.68: Some of the heads of the family lines, when they got back to the Lord's house in Jerusalem, gave freely to help rebuild it.
2.69: They dropped 61,000 gold coins, 5,000 silver minas, and 100 sets of priest robes into the treasury—whatever they could spare.
2.70: So the priests, Levites, some of the people, singers, gatekeepers, and Temple workers settled in their towns. All of Israel got back to living in their own cities.

3.1: When the seventh month rolled around and everybody was settled in their cities, the people came together like one big family in Jerusalem.
3.2: Then Jeshua, son of Jozadak, and his priest fam, along with Zerubbabel, son of Shealtiel, and his crew, got up and rebuilt the altar of the God of Israel. They had to bring the burnt offerings like Moses laid out in the Law.
3.3: Even though they were nervous 'cause of the folks from the other nations around 'em, they still set the altar back in place and started offering burnt sacrifices—every morning and every evening, just like clockwork.
3.4: They kept the Feast of Tabernacles too, just like the Scriptures said. Brought those daily offerings, exactly how it was supposed to be done each day.
3.5: After that, they kept up with the regular burnt offerings, the ones for the new moons, the special feasts the Lord set aside, and any freewill offerings folks wanted to give. They wasn't missing nothin'.
3.6: From the first day of that seventh month, they started offering burnt sacrifices to the Lord—even though the temple's foundation hadn't even been laid yet.
3.7: They put money in the hands of the masons and carpenters, and gave food, drinks, and oil to the folks in Sidon and Tyre so they could ship cedar logs from Lebanon down to Joppa. They had the green light from King Cyrus of Persia.
3.8: By the second month of the second year after they got back to God's house in Jerusalem, Zerubbabel, Jeshua, the priests, the Levites, and everybody who came outta exile started the work. They picked Levites 20 years and up to run things at the Lord's house.
3.9: Jeshua and his fam, Kadmiel and his fam, plus the sons of Judah and the crew from Henadad's family—all of 'em Levites—stepped up together to lead the rebuild.
3.10: When the builders finally laid the foundation of the Lord's temple, the priests showed up in their robes with trumpets, and the Levites from Asaph's line had cymbals. They praised the Lord just like King David had set up back in the day.
3.11: They sang back and forth to each other, giving God thanks and shouting praise: 'He's good! His mercy don't ever run out when it come to Israel!' Everybody turned up—loud shoutin', full praise—'cause the foundation was finally laid.
3.12: But some of the old heads—the priests, Levites, and elders—who remembered the first temple? They started cryin' loud when they saw this new one's foundation. Still, a lot of folks were shoutin' with joy at the same time.
3.13: It got so wild, you couldn't even tell who was cryin' and who was celebratin'. The sound was so loud, folks could hear it way off in the distance.

4.1: When the enemies of Judah and Benjamin heard that the folks who came back from exile were rebuilding the temple of the Lord God of Israel, they started schemin'.
4.2: They rolled up on Zerubbabel and the family heads and said, 'Let us help y'all build! We worship your God too—we been offering sacrifices to Him ever since King Esarhaddon of Assyria brought us here.'
4.3: But Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the rest of Israel's leaders were like, 'Nah—we got this. Y'all not helpin' us build the house for our God. King Cyrus of Persia gave us the assignment, so we doin' it ourselves.'
4.4: After that, the locals did everything they could to discourage the people of Judah—had 'em stressed out and shook while tryin' to build.
4.5: They even hired lawyers and advisors to block the project, tryna mess it up from Cyrus' time all the way through King Darius' reign.
4.6: During King Ahasuerus' reign, early on, they wrote up a whole complaint against the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
4.7: Later, during the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabel, and their crew wrote to the king. The letter was in Aramaic, and they made sure it got translated properly.
4.8: Rehum the governor and Shimshai the secretary wrote a letter straight up against Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes.
4.9: It came from Rehum, Shimshai, and the rest of their clique—folks from Dinah, Apharsath, Tarpel, Persia, Erech, Babylon, Shushan, Dehav, Elam—basically all the nations that Osnapper had relocated to Samaria and the region beyond the River.
4.10: All them people were part of the mix, brought over by that big-shot Osnapper who had moved a whole bunch of nations into the area.
4.11: Here's a copy of what they wrote: 'To King Artaxerxes—peace and blessings from your loyal folks out here beyond the River.'
4.12: 'Let it be known, King: them Jews you sent back here? They settin' up shop in Jerusalem, that rebellious and wicked city. They buildin' it up again—walls and foundations included.'
4.13: 'You should know—if they finish this city and them walls go up, they won't be payin' no taxes, tributes, or customs. Your pockets gon' feel it, Your Majesty.'
4.14: 'Since we got love for the palace and don't wanna see the king take an L, we figured we better speak up and put you on game.'
4.15: 'Check the history books from your ancestors—you'll see this city been on some rebellious stuff, stirrin' up problems for kings and regions. That's why it got destroyed in the first place.'
4.16: 'So just so you know, if this place gets rebuilt and the walls go up, you ain't gon' have no control left out here beyond the River.'
4.17: King Artaxerxes sent back a response: 'To Rehum the governor, Shimshai the secretary, and all y'all folks livin' out in Samaria and beyond the River—peace.'
4.18: 'That letter y'all sent? I read it loud and clear.'
4.19: 'I had my people dig into the records, and yep—it's true. This city got a whole track record of rebellion, trouble, and starting uprisings against kings.'
4.20: 'Back in the day, strong kings ruled from Jerusalem. They ran the whole region beyond the River, and people used to pay them taxes and tributes.'
4.21: 'So here's the order—shut that whole rebuild down. Don't let 'em lift another brick till I say otherwise.'
4.22: 'Make sure this happens quick. Why let this mess grow and come back to bite the throne?'
4.23: Soon as Rehum, Shimshai, and their folks read the king's letter, they rushed down to Jerusalem and rolled up on the Jews with force. Shut it down, hard.
4.24: So the work on God's house in Jerusalem stopped. It stayed on pause until the second year of King Darius of Persia.

5.1: Then the prophets Haggai and Zechariah (son of Iddo) spoke out to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem, givin' them a word straight from the God of Israel who was still watchin' over them.
5.2: So Zerubbabel (son of Shealtiel) and Jeshua (son of Jozadak) got up and started buildin' God's house again in Jerusalem. And the prophets? They was right there with 'em, holdin' it down and helpin' out.
5.3: But at that same time, Tattenai—the governor from across the River—showed up with Shethar-Boznai and their crew. They pulled up askin': 'Who told y'all to start buildin' this temple and fixin' up these walls?'
5.4: So we gave 'em the names of the men leadin' the project, lettin' 'em know who was really puttin' in work.
5.5: But God had His eyes on the elders of the Jews, so they didn't get shut down right away. They had to wait for word to go back to King Darius—and for a response to come back.
5.6: Here's a copy of the letter Tattenai sent to King Darius, with Shethar-Boznai and all the other Persian officials from the region beyond the River co-signin' it.
5.7: They wrote: 'To King Darius—peace and respect.'
5.8: 'We need to let you know, we went over to Judea and checked out the temple of the great God. They buildin' it strong—usin' big stones and timber for the walls. And they ain't slackin'—the work movin' fast and steady in their hands.'
5.9: 'We asked the elders: "Who gave y'all permission to build this temple and finish the walls?"'
5.10: 'We also asked for the names of the men in charge, so we could write it all down and let you know exactly who's behind this.'
5.11: 'Here's what they told us: "We servants of the God of heaven and earth. We rebuildin' the temple that was here long ago—the one a great king of Israel built and finished."'
5.12: '"But our ancestors made God mad—real mad—so He let Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon (a Chaldean), take us down. He tore the temple up and took the people into captivity."'
5.13: '"But in the first year Cyrus became king over Babylon, he gave the go-ahead to rebuild God's house."'
5.14: '"And the gold and silver stuff from the temple that Nebuchadnezzar had stolen—Cyrus gave that back too. He handed it over to a man named Sheshbazzar, who he put in charge as governor."'
5.15: '"Cyrus told him: 'Take all these items, head back to Jerusalem, and rebuild the temple on its old spot.'"'
5.16: '"So Sheshbazzar came through, laid the foundation, and started the build. They been workin' on it ever since, but it ain't finished yet."'
5.17: 'So if the king cool with it, we ask that you search the archives up in Babylon to see if King Cyrus really gave that order. Then let us know what the king wanna do next.'

6.1: So King Darius put out an order, and they started searchin' through the records stored with the treasures in Babylon.
6.2: They found a scroll in the palace at Achmetha, up in the province of Media, and this what it said:
6.3: 'In the first year of King Cyrus, he gave this decree: The temple of God in Jerusalem gotta be rebuilt—the place where they give sacrifices. Set the foundation strong. It should be 60 cubits high and 60 wide.'
6.4: 'Use three layers of big stone blocks and one layer of fresh timber. And don't worry about the money—it's comin' from the king's own funds.'
6.5: 'Also, bring back the gold and silver items Nebuchadnezzar stole from the temple in Jerusalem. Take 'em back to their rightful spots in the house of God.'
6.6: So now, Tattenai, governor across the River, Shethar-Boznai, and y'all crew—fall back. Don't mess with 'em.
6.7: Let the governor of the Jews and the elders handle they business. Let 'em build God's house right there where it belongs.
6.8: I'm also makin' a new decree: Help these elders out! Fund it with tax money from your region across the River. No delays, pay up!
6.9: Whatever they need—young bulls, rams, lambs for sacrifices, wheat, salt, wine, oil—whatever the priests ask for, give it to 'em every day, no excuses.
6.10: So they can keep the sacrifices goin' and pray for me and my sons too. I need that blessing.
6.11: And let me be clear—if anybody tries to change this order, snatch wood from their house, stand it up, and hang 'em on it. Then turn their whole crib into a pile of trash.
6.12: May the same God who lives in that temple tear down any king or nation that tries to stop or destroy this house. I, Darius, said it. Don't play—get it done.
6.13: So Tattenai, Shethar-Boznai, and their folks followed every word King Darius said. They ain't drag they feet.
6.14: The Jewish elders kept on buildin', encouraged by the words of Haggai and Zechariah. They finished the temple just like God told 'em to—plus the commands from Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes.
6.15: They wrapped it up on the third day of the month Adar, in year six of King Darius' rule.
6.16: Everybody who came back from exile—the Israelites, the priests, the Levites—celebrated the temple's dedication with pure joy.
6.17: They offered a hundred bulls, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs, and twelve male goats for sin offerings—one goat for each tribe of Israel.
6.18: They got the priests and Levites back into their proper roles to serve in God's house, just like Moses laid out.
6.19: The returnees kept the Passover on the 14th day of the first month.
6.20: The priests and Levites had purified themselves—all of 'em was clean. They sacrificed the Passover lambs for the whole crew, the priests, and themselves.
6.21: The Israelites who came back from exile ate together with everybody who had turned away from the nastiness of the surrounding nations and came to seek the Lord, the God of Israel.
6.22: Then they kept the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven whole days—full of joy. The Lord made 'em glad and even moved the heart of the king of Assyria to support the work they was doin' for the house of God, the God of Israel.

7.1: After all that, during the reign of King Artaxerxes of Persia, a man named Ezra showed up—son of Seraiah, grandson of Azariah, great-grandson of Hilkiah,
7.2: descendant of Shallum, Zadok, and Ahitub,
7.3: from the line of Amariah, Azariah, and Meraioth,
7.5: son of Abishua, son of Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron—the high priest himself.
7.6: Ezra came from Babylon, and he was cold with it—knew the Law of Moses front to back, the Law God gave to Israel. The king gave Ezra whatever he asked for, 'cause God had His hand all over him.
7.7: Some Israelites, along with priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, and temple workers came with Ezra in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes' reign.
7.8: Ezra got to Jerusalem in the fifth month of that same seventh year.
7.9: He left Babylon on the first day of the first month, and showed up in Jerusalem by the first day of the fifth—'cause God's hand was still on him.
7.10: Ezra came prepared. His heart was locked in to learn God's Law, live it out, and teach it to the people—statutes and all.
7.11: This right here is a copy of the letter King Artaxerxes gave to Ezra, the priest and Law scholar—an expert in the commandments of the Lord and His rules for Israel:
7.12: 'Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra the priest and Law scribe of the God of heaven—peace and blessings.'
7.13: 'I'm making it official: any of the Israelites, priests, or Levites who wanna roll with you back to Jerusalem—let 'em go.'
7.14: 'You goin' out on royal business—you and my seven advisors. Y'all check up on Judah and Jerusalem, according to the Law of your God that you carry.'
7.15: 'And you gon' take the silver and gold we're givin' freely to the God of Israel, whose house is in Jerusalem.'
7.16: 'Plus, whatever silver and gold you gather up in Babylon—along with the freewill offerings from the people and priests—bring that too. It's all for God's house.'
7.17: 'Use that money wisely—buy bulls, rams, and lambs with their grain and drink offerings, and present 'em on God's altar in Jerusalem.'
7.18: 'And whatever else you and your crew feel led to do with the leftover money—do it according to your God's will.'
7.19: 'Also, all the sacred articles for temple use—make sure they get delivered to God's house in full.'
7.20: 'If you need anything else for the temple, take care of it with funds from the king's treasury.'
7.21: 'I, King Artaxerxes, now declare to all my treasurers beyond the River—whatever Ezra the priest asks for, give it to him, and don't slack.'
7.22: 'Up to 100 talents of silver, 100 kors of wheat, 100 baths of wine and oil, and unlimited salt—no cap.'
7.23: 'Do whatever the God of heaven commands. We not tryin' to catch no wrath from Him—especially not on me or my sons.'
7.24: 'And just so y'all know—no taxes, tribute, or customs can be charged on any priest, Levite, singer, gatekeeper, temple servant, or temple worker. Don't even try it.'
7.25: 'Ezra, based on the wisdom your God gave you, appoint judges and leaders for all the people beyond the River—everybody who knows the Law. And for those who don't? Teach 'em.'
7.26: 'Whoever refuses to follow God's Law—or the king's—handle that. Give 'em what they got comin': death, exile, property taken, or jail. Handle business quick.'
7.27: Bless the Lord, God of our ancestors! He put it on the king's heart to upgrade God's house in Jerusalem.
7.28: God showed me so much favor in front of the king, his advisors, and all the royal bosses—I was encouraged, 'cause the Lord had His hand on me. So I rounded up some top men from Israel to roll with me.

8.1: These the family heads and genealogies of the folks that came up with me from Babylon during the time of King Artaxerxes:
8.2: From Phinehas' line: Gershom. From Ithamar's: Daniel. From David's: Hattush.
8.3: From Shecaniah's people—descendants of Parosh: Zechariah, rollin' deep with 150 men.
8.4: From Pahath-Moab's family: Eliehoenai son of Zerahiah, and 200 men.
8.5: From Shecaniah's line: Ben-Jahaziel and 300 men.
8.6: From Adin's fam: Ebed son of Jonathan, with 50 men.
8.7: From Elam: Jeshaiah son of Athaliah, with 70 men.
8.8: From Shephatiah's crew: Zebadiah son of Michael, with 80 men.
8.9: From Joab's family: Obadiah son of Jehiel, with 218 men.
8.10: From Shelomith's people: Ben-Josiphiah, and 160 men.
8.11: From Bebai's folks: Zechariah son of Bebai, and 28 men.
8.12: From Azgad's family: Johanan son of Hakkatan, and 110 men.
8.13: From Adonikam's last crew: Eliphelet, Jeiel, and Shemaiah—with 60 men.
8.14: From Bigvai's people: Uthai and Zabbud—with 70 men.
8.15: I gathered the squad by the river that flows to Ahava, and we camped there for three days. I looked around and noticed—no Levites showed up.
8.16: So I sent for Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, another Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah, and Meshullam—some leaders—and also Joiarib and Elnathan (again), who had sense.
8.17: I gave 'em instructions to go talk to Iddo, the head man at Casiphia, and tell him and his temple servants to send us folks to help out with God's house.
8.18: Thanks to God's favor, they sent us a wise man—Sherebiah, from the line of Mahli, who was from Levi, son of Israel—along with his sons and brothers, 18 men.
8.19: Then came Hashabiah and Jeshaiah from the sons of Merari, with their kin—20 more men.
8.20: And 220 temple servants (Nethinim), the same ones King David and the leaders had assigned to help the Levites. They was all listed by name.
8.21: Then I called a fast by the river of Ahava, so we could humble ourselves before God and ask Him to guide us, our kids, and all our stuff safely.
8.22: I didn't wanna ask the king for soldiers or bodyguards on the way, 'cause we had already told him, 'God looks out for those who seek Him, but His power and anger hit hard on the ones who don't.'
8.23: So we fasted and prayed—and God came through for us.
8.24: I chose 12 priests to handle the goods—Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and 10 of their brothers.
8.25: I weighed out the silver, gold, and articles for God's house—offerings from the king, his officials, and the Israelites who had showed up.
8.26: I put in their hands: 650 talents of silver, 100 silver items weighin' another 100 talents, and 100 talents of gold.
8.27: Also 20 gold bowls worth a thousand coins, and two polished bronze items that shined like gold.
8.28: I told 'em, 'Y'all and these items are holy to the Lord. This silver and gold is a freewill gift to the God of our ancestors.'
8.29: 'Guard it all real careful until y'all weigh it again in front of the leaders, priests, Levites, and heads of Israel's families when we get to Jerusalem, inside God's house.'
8.30: So the priests and Levites took the goods by weight, ready to deliver it to God's house in Jerusalem.
8.31: We left the river Ahava on the twelfth day of the first month, headin' to Jerusalem. God had His hand on us, and we didn't get jumped by enemies or ambushes along the way.
8.32: We made it to Jerusalem and chilled for three days.
8.33: On day four, everything—silver, gold, and all the items—was weighed at God's house. Meremoth son of Uriah the priest handled it, along with Eleazar son of Phinehas. Jozabad (son of Jeshua) and Noadiah (son of Binnui), both Levites, were with them.
8.34: Everything was counted and weighed properly. It all got recorded that same day.
8.35: The ones who came outta captivity gave burnt offerings to the God of Israel: 12 bulls for the 12 tribes, 96 rams, 77 lambs, and 12 male goats as a sin offering. They offered all of it to the Lord.
8.36: Then we handed over the king's orders to his officials and the local governors across the River. They gave us their support—and backed God's house too.

9.1: After all that got handled, the leaders came to me talkin' 'bout, 'Ezra, the people of Israel—including the priests and Levites—ain't been keepin' they distance from the folks in these other lands. They out here messin' with the same detestable ways of the Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites, Ammonites, Moabites, Egyptians, and Amorites.'
9.2: 'They even married their daughters and let their sons do the same—so now the holy line, the chosen seed, all mixed up with the other nations. And worst part? It's the leaders and top folks who started this mess.'
9.3: When I heard that, I straight up tore my robe and tunic, yanked out hair from my head and beard, and just sat there—shook.
9.4: Everybody who still feared the words of the God of Israel came and sat with me, 'cause of how wild the exiles had gone. I just sat there stunned until the evening sacrifice.
9.5: When it was time for the evening sacrifice, I got up from my grieving, clothes still torn, dropped to my knees, and stretched out my hands to the Lord my God.
9.6: I said, 'God… I can't even lift my head. I'm ashamed and embarrassed to come to You like this. Our sins? They so deep, they over our heads. Our guilt reachin' all the way to the heavens.'
9.7: 'Since way back—our ancestors' time till now—we been messin' up. That's why we, our kings, and our priests got handed over to other nations. We faced the sword, got taken into exile, got robbed, and straight humiliated—just like today.'
9.8: 'But now, for just a moment, You done showed us grace, Lord. You let a small remnant survive, gave us a little stake in Your holy place, and brought some light back into our eyes. Gave us a lil' life even while we still in chains.'
9.9: 'Yeah, we was slaves, but You ain't forget about us. You touched the hearts of the Persian kings to show us favor—let us rebuild Your house, fix what was broken, and even put up a wall in Judah and Jerusalem.'
9.10: 'But now, God… what can we even say? We've been breakin' Your commandments again.'
9.11: 'The ones You gave through Your prophets sayin': "The land y'all goin' into is messed up—it's spiritually dirty from one end to the other because of the nasty ways of the folks already there."'
9.12: 'You told us: "Don't let your daughters marry their sons or your sons marry their daughters. Don't go seekin' their peace or blessings. That way, you'll stay strong, enjoy the land's goodness, and leave it to your children as an inheritance forever."'
9.13: 'After everything You've let happen to us 'cause of our mess—and even then You went easy on us and still gave us a chance like this—'
9.14: 'Should we really break Your rules again? Go mixin' with the same people doin' the stuff You hate? Wouldn't You be right to wipe us out completely—no remnant, no survivors?'
9.15: 'Lord God of Israel, You always do right. That's why we still here as a small leftover group. But we guilty. And honestly? We can't even stand in front of You like this.'

10.1: While Ezra was down on his knees prayin', cryin', and confessin' in front of God's house, a huge crowd showed up—men, women, and kids from all over Israel. Everybody was cryin' their eyes out.
10.2: Then Shechaniah, son of Jehiel (from Elam's fam), spoke up: 'We messed up, man. We married women from the surrounding nations, and that ain't what God wanted. But even after this, there's still hope for Israel.'
10.3: 'So let's make a deal with God right now. We gon' send away these foreign wives and their kids—do it just like you and all who fear God's commandments are sayin', and let's do it by the Law.'
10.4: 'Ezra, this your lane. Stand up and handle it. We got your back—be strong and go do it.'
10.5: So Ezra stood up and made the leaders—priests, Levites, and all Israel—swear they would follow through. And they all took that oath.
10.6: Ezra left God's house and went to Jehohanan's room (he was Eliashib's son). He didn't eat or drink nothin'—he was in deep grief over how the exiles had turned their backs on God.
10.7: Then they sent out word all across Judah and Jerusalem, tellin' everybody from the exile crew to show up in Jerusalem.
10.8: Anybody who ain't show up in three days? They were gettin' cut off—property taken, and they wouldn't be part of the community anymore.
10.9: So everybody from Judah and Benjamin pulled up in three days. It was the 20th day of the ninth month. They were all sittin' in the open square near God's house, shakin' from the situation—and from the heavy rain.
10.10: Ezra stood up and said, 'Y'all crossed the line. You took foreign wives and added to Israel's guilt.'
10.11: 'So now—own up to it. Confess to the Lord, the God of your ancestors. Do what He says. Separate yourselves from the people of this land—and from those wives.'
10.12: The whole assembly shouted back, 'Yes, sir! You right—we gon' do it just like you said!'
10.13: 'But there's a lotta us, and it's pourin' rain out here. This ain't a one-day fix—too many of us are involved.'
10.14: 'Let our leaders step up for the whole group, and let the guilty men in each town come at scheduled times with their elders and judges, until God's anger calms down.'
10.15: Only Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahaziah son of Tikvah disagreed—and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite backed 'em up.
10.16: But the rest of the exiles followed through. Ezra the priest selected family heads, one from each house, listed by name. They started sittin' down to handle it on the first day of the tenth month.
10.17: And by the first day of the first month, they were done talkin' with every man who had married a foreign wife.
10.18: From the priests: From Jeshua (son of Jozadak) and his brothers—Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib, and Gedaliah.
10.19: They promised to send their wives away, and offered a ram from the flock for their guilt.
10.20: From Immer's line: Hanani and Zebadiah.
10.21: From Harim's: Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah.
10.22: From Pashhur's: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Elasah.
10.23: From the Levites: Jozabad, Shimei, Kelaiah (aka Kelita), Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer.
10.24: From the singers: Eliashib. From the gatekeepers: Shallum, Telem, and Uri.
10.25: Parosh's family: Ramiah, Jeziah, Malchiah, Mijamin, Eleazar, Malchijah, and Benaiah.
10.26: Elam's: Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth, and Eliah.
10.27: Zattu's: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad, and Aziza.
10.28: Bebai's: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, and Athlai.
10.29: Bani's: Meshullam, Malluch, Adaiah, Jashub, Sheal, and Ramoth.
10.30: Pahath-Moab's: Adna, Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui, and Manasseh.
10.31: Harim's: Eliezer, Ishijah, Malchijah, Shemaiah, Shimeon,
10.33: Hashum's: Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, and Shimei.
10.43: From Nebo's fam: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jaddai, Joel, and Benaiah.
10.44: All these men had taken foreign wives—and some of those wives had given them children.
